title: Boogiepop Doesn't Laugh
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: At Shinyo Academy, girls are disappearing; teachers assume runaways, but students whisper about Boogiepop, an urban-legend 'angel of death' who may be the alter ego of a student. Told by several students whose accounts overlap and conflict, the two-volume manga adaptation of Kouhei Kadono's novel pieces together a mystery involving a creature that devours schoolgirls, a new drug and a past serial killer.
life_message: Ordinary lives hide great dangers and meanings, and truth must be pieced together from many points of view.

content.note: Murders, a creature devouring dead schoolgirls; review says 'startling but not particularly grisly' (MU Murder, Violence, Serial Killer).
Dark, moody horror mystery; disappearances (review; MU Dark Ambience; AniList Supernatural).
Creature shown as a naked woman (review; MU Nudity; AniList Nudity tag low). Student romance subplot.
A new drug in the plot (AniList description; MU Drug/s).
Suicide of a serial killer referenced (review); alter egos and dissociation (AniList Dissociative Identities; MU Alter Ego).

dominant: Fragmented truth and perspective; adolescent identity; death and the uncanny

folkways.japan: Urban legends (toshi densetsu) spreading among schoolgirls and a shinigami figure draw on Japanese folklore and school culture.

delivery.evidence: Review: 'up to the reader to solve the puzzle'; Rashomon-like conflicting narrators.
delivery.note: Meaning is left to readers, who must assemble conflicting accounts; Boogiepop is 'either a savior or a demon, depending on who is talking.'

winners_losers: Ambiguous: Boogiepop's role as protector or demon depends on the narrator; victims are schoolgirls.
